title: The People of ’Ad
hook: A people amplified in strength asked who could be mightier, and the wind answered for seven nights and eight days.
body: After the people of Nuh had passed, the Qur’an says, Allah made ’Ad successors in the earth and increased them abundantly in stature and strength. To them He sent their brother Hud, who asked nothing but that they worship Allah alone and remember the favor that had raised them. Their answer was the boast the Qur’an preserves, who is mightier than us in strength, and its reply is immediate: the One who created them is mightier. They clung to what their fathers served, and the argument closed with a promise of punishment they had dared their prophet to hasten.

The end came by wind, a barren, screaming wind that Allah imposed on them seven nights and eight days without pause. Surah al-Haqqah lets us see the morning after: a people thrown down as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees, and asks whether any remnant of them can be found. Surah al-Fajr names their glory, Iram of the pillars, the like of which had not been created in the lands, and al-Ahqaf names their home among the wind curved dunes. Strength, the passage teaches, is an argument for the Maker, never against Him.

How tall were they? The Qur’an says only that their creation was amplified, and it lets that suffice. Later reports circulated exact figures in cubits, sometimes vast ones, yet these travel through chains and lore whose soundness is debated, not through the Book or the established Sunnah, and this room does not state them as fact. What is established is the lesson ’Ad were built to carry: no measure of body or building has ever held back the command of Allah.

claims.text: Allah made ’Ad successors after the people of Nuh and increased them abundantly in stature and strength
They were destroyed by a furious, barren wind imposed on them seven nights and eight days, leaving them like hollow trunks of palm trees
Iram of the pillars, the like of which had not been created in the lands, names their glory
Exact heights in cubits for ’Ad circulate only in later reports and are not stated here as fact

evidence.boundary: The sources give no measurements for ’Ad, no location for Iram beyond the homeland at al-Ahqaf, and no surviving ruin identified with them; matching Iram to any excavated site is not established.
evidence.note: Qur’an 46:21 places Hud’s warning at al-Ahqaf, the region of the dunes; that is as far as the map goes.

title: Thamud and the She-Camel
hook: To a people who carved mountains into homes, Allah sent a she-camel as a test, and one cry ended the trial.
body: Thamud rose after ’Ad, settled where plains gave them palaces and mountains gave them carved houses, and to them Allah sent their brother Salih. When they demanded proof, the proof came walking: the she-camel of Allah, a clear sign from their Lord. The command was gentle and exact, let her eat in Allah’s earth, the water is shared between her and you, and do not touch her with harm. Surah ash-Shams tells the ending in five verses: the most wretched of them rose, the she-camel was hamstrung, and their Lord crushed them for their sin and made them level.

Surah al-Hijr calls them the companions of al-Hijr, who denied the messengers and carved secure homes from the mountains, till the cry seized them at morning and nothing they had earned availed them. Surah Hud adds the mercy inside the warning: after the she-camel was hamstrung they were granted three days in their homes, a promise not to be belied. Security cut from rock, the passage teaches, is still only rock; the only safety that morning belonged to Salih and those who believed with him.

Centuries later, on the road to Tabuk, the Prophet ﷺ passed the dwellings at al-Hijr and told his companions not to enter upon the punished people except weeping, lest what struck them strike those who pass. The place is identified with the site now called Mada’in Salih in northwest Arabia, an editorial note from geography rather than revelation, and archaeologists date its standing rock cut facades to the later Nabataean period. The stone remembers builders; the Qur’an remembers why building was not enough.

claims.text: The she-camel was sent as a clear sign and a trial, the water divided between her and them, and they hamstrung her
They carved secure homes from the mountains, and the cry seized them at morning after three days of respite
Passing al-Hijr, the Prophet ﷺ told his companions not to enter upon the punished people except weeping

Mada’in Salih in northwest Arabia is identified with al-Hijr, while its standing rock cut facades are dated by archaeologists to the later Nabataean period, so no visible structure is attributed to Thamud

evidence.boundary: The sources do not date Thamud, do not describe the she-camel beyond her being a sign with a right to water, and do not tie any particular surviving facade to them.
evidence.note: The punishment is called a quake in 7:78 and a cry in 11:67; mufassirin read these as one seizure described from two sides.

title: Yajuj and Majuj
hook: Behind a wall of iron and molten copper waits a people whose release is written among the last promises.
body: In Surah al-Kahf, Dhul-Qarnayn reaches a people between two mountain walls who can barely understand speech, and they plead for help against Yajuj and Majuj, corrupters in the land. He refuses their payment, asks instead for strength of hands, and builds: blocks of iron filling the gap, bellows worked until the metal glows like fire, molten copper poured over the whole. The Qur’an records the result and its limit in one breath, they could not climb over it and they could not pierce it, then his own words: this is a mercy from my Lord, and when my Lord’s promise comes, He will level it.

Their release belongs to the grammar of the end. Surah al-Anbiya binds it to the approach of the true promise: when Yajuj and Majuj are opened and they slide down from every height, the eyes of the disbelievers will stare. In Muslim 2937 they emerge after Isa ﷺ has descended and the Dajjal is gone, a host no one has power to fight, ended not by armies but by Allah’s command. And when Bukhari 3348 describes the delegation of the Fire, nine hundred ninety nine of every thousand, the Prophet ﷺ comforted his companions that the count is filled from Yajuj and Majuj, one man of you beside a thousand of them.

A narration in Tirmidhi describes them digging at the barrier each day until they nearly see sunlight, told to return tomorrow, and finding it restored, until the day their leader adds, if Allah wills, and it stands as they left it, and they break out. Scholars have discussed this report’s grading and its fit with the verse that they could not pierce the barrier, so this room cites it as a report, not a certainty. Where the barrier stands, what they look like, and how many they are, the sources leave unsaid, and we leave it unsaid with them.

claims.text: Dhul-Qarnayn built a barrier of iron and molten copper that Yajuj and Majuj could neither scale nor pierce, and when Allah’s promise comes He will level it
Their opening, hastening down from every height, is bound to the drawing near of the true promise
They emerge after the descent of Isa ﷺ and are ended by Allah’s command, not by human strength

In the hadith of the delegation of the Fire, nine hundred and ninety nine of every thousand, the Prophet ﷺ comforted his companions that the number is filled from Yajuj and Majuj, one man of you beside a thousand of them

evidence.boundary: The sources assign them no faces, no sizes, and no census, and they fix no map reference; identifying the barrier with any known wall, or them with any modern nation, is not established.
evidence.note: The report of daily digging at the barrier is cited from Tirmidhi as a report; its grading is discussed among hadith scholars, and the Qur’an’s wording that they could not pierce it stands as revealed.

title: The People of Nuh and the Long Patience
hook: Nine hundred and fifty years of calling ended with a door that closed as the sky’s gates opened.
body: The Qur’an gives the span itself: Nuh remained among his people a thousand years less fifty, calling them to their Lord. Surah Nuh preserves the shape of that patience, I called them night and day, openly and in secret; they pressed their fingers into their ears and pulled their garments over themselves and grew arrogant. He promised them what repentance buys, forgiveness, rain in abundance, wealth and sons, gardens and rivers. Generations were born, heard the same truthful voice, and taught their children to refuse it, clinging to Wadd and Suwa and the idols the Qur’an names.

Surah al-Qamar carries the ending in a rush of verses: they called Our servant a liar and said, madman, and he was rebuked, so he called his Lord, I am overcome, so give victory. Then the gates of the sky were opened with pouring water and the earth burst with springs, and the waters met by a decree already measured. Nuh was carried on a thing of planks and nails, running under Our eyes, a recompense for the one denied. Of his people the Qur’an says they were drowned for their sins and made to enter a Fire; it was left as a sign, the surah says, so is there any who will remember?

How far did the water reach? The Qur’an fixes the moral scope with perfect clarity, the people who denied Nuh were destroyed, none of the believers were lost, and Nuh prayed that no dweller from the disbelievers be left upon the earth. What it does not give is a map. Whether the flood covered the whole planet or the whole of Nuh’s people and their lands is a question scholars have discussed, and this entry marks it debated rather than deciding it. The certainty is the lesson: denial drowned, and gratitude sailed.

claims.text: Nuh remained among his people a thousand years less fifty, and the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers
He called them night and day, openly and in secret, and they pressed their fingers into their ears and persisted in arrogance
The sky’s gates were opened with pouring water, the earth burst with springs, and Nuh was carried on a vessel of planks and nails, left as a sign
Whether the flood covered the entire earth or encompassed the people of Nuh and their lands is discussed among scholars; the Qur’an states who was destroyed, not the flood’s map

evidence.boundary: The sources do not give the flood’s geography or the ark’s dimensions, and beyond the name al-Judi they do not locate its resting place; counts of those aboard come from reports, not the Qur’an.
evidence.note: Qur’an 11:40 says only that those who believed with him were few.

title: Dabbat al-Ard, the Beast of the Earth
hook: Of all the signs, this one is a single verse: the earth gives up a creature, and it speaks.
body: Surah an-Naml holds the entire Qur’anic knowledge of this sign in one verse. When the word falls due upon people, Allah says, We shall bring out for them a creature from the earth that will speak to them, because people were not certain of Our signs. Every element is weighed: it comes when the sentence has already fallen, it is brought out, not born of human plans, it is from the earth itself, and its work is speech, an address to a humanity that ran out of certainty. The verse gives no shape, no size, no species, and no place.

The Sunnah confirms its rank. In Muslim 2901 the Beast stands among the ten great signs the Hour will not arrive without, and in Muslim 158 it is named with the Dajjal and the sun rising from its west among signs after which faith no longer benefits a soul that had not believed before. Everything else, its form, its tools, the reports that it marks the faces of believers and disbelievers, comes through narrations whose grading scholars dispute, and through tafsir traditions of uneven strength. This room records that material as claimed, not as known.

A rule of this room follows from that honesty: the Beast is never illustrated here, and no animal form is assigned to it. Where later pages painted composite creatures, the Qur’an chose restraint, and restraint is part of the sign’s power. What is certain is the order and the meaning: it comes when the word has already fallen due, and once it speaks, the age of arguing about the unseen is over.

claims.text: When the word falls due upon people, a creature from the earth is brought out that speaks to them, because people were not certain of Allah’s signs
The Beast is one of the ten great signs before the Hour
It is named with the Dajjal and the western sunrise among signs after which faith no longer benefits one who had not believed before
Its form, size, place of emergence, and the marking of faces come from reports and tafsir traditions whose grading is disputed

evidence.boundary: The sources do not establish what the Beast looks like, where it emerges, or its species; reports naming particular features or places are disputed and are not stated as fact.
evidence.note: Rule of this room: no illustration or animal form is ever assigned to the Beast, because the Qur’an assigns none.

title: The Smoke
hook: Between a famine remembered and a sign still awaited stands one verse of smoke that covers the people.
body: So watch, Surah ad-Dukhan commands, for a day when the sky brings a visible smoke that envelops the people; this is a painful punishment. The next verse records the plea it will draw out, our Lord, remove the punishment from us, we are believers, and the answer asks how they will remember now, when a clear Messenger already came and was turned away. The scene is brief and vivid: a sky that testifies, a people wrapped in what they cannot argue with, and a plea arriving late.

Here the mufassirin genuinely part ways, and this room shows both paths. Ibn Mas’ud, in narrations recorded by Bukhari, held that the smoke had already passed: when Quraysh refused, the Prophet ﷺ prayed against them with years like the years of Yusuf, and hunger thinned the world until a man looked at the sky and saw something like smoke; among five signs he counted as passed was the smoke. Other companions and early scholars held that the smoke is still ahead, a real covering of the sky among the last signs, and the Prophet’s ﷺ list of ten signs before the Hour in Muslim 2901 includes the Smoke.

Some scholars reconcile the two, a smoke that touched Quraysh as a foretaste and a greater smoke to come; others keep to one side. This entry does not force the verdict. What can be said with a clear conscience is this: the verse is certain, the command to watch is certain, the Smoke appears in the Prophet’s ﷺ list of great signs, and the exact placement between past and future is a matter the earliest readers of the verse already discussed.

claims.text: The Qur’an commands watching for a day when the sky brings a visible smoke that covers the people, called a painful punishment
The Smoke is named in the ten great signs before the Hour
Whether the verse was fulfilled in the famine that pressed Quraysh, as Ibn Mas’ud explained, or awaits fulfillment as a future sign, or both, is a standing discussion among the mufassirin

evidence.boundary: The sources do not fix the Smoke’s timing, duration, or cause, and identifying it with any modern haze, eruption, or event is not established.
evidence.note: Read 44:10-16 whole: the plea to lift the punishment, the reminder of a clear Messenger turned away, and the day of the greatest seizing.

title: The Sun Rising from Its Setting Place
hook: One morning the sun will rise where it has always set, and the longest open door in creation will close.
body: The Prophet ﷺ said that the Hour will not stand until the sun rises from its setting place; when it rises and the people see it, all of them will believe, and that is the moment when faith benefits no soul that had not believed before or earned good in its faith. Bukhari places the report under the verse of al-An’am it echoes, the day some of your Lord’s signs come, and the narration itself recites it. Nothing in creation’s routine is more trusted than the sun’s path; the sign is precisely the breaking of the world’s most reliable habit.

Why this sign closes the door, the Sunnah explains elsewhere: Allah extends His hand by night to accept the repentance of the day’s sinner, and extends His hand by day to accept the repentance of the night’s sinner, until the sun rises from its west. Repentance lives while the world’s order holds; a sunrise from the west announces that the order is being folded away. Muslim 2901 counts this among the ten great signs, and Muslim 158 groups it with the Dajjal and the Beast as the signs after which belief no longer avails one who had not believed.

claims.text: The Hour will not stand until the sun rises from its setting place; when the people see it, all will believe, at the moment faith no longer benefits one who had not believed before
Allah extends His hand by night and by day to accept repentance until the sun rises from its west
The narration itself joins this sign to the verse, the day some of your Lord’s signs come, no soul will benefit from its faith

evidence.boundary: The sources do not give a date, a mechanism, or a picture of that morning beyond the rising itself; astronomical speculation is not part of the evidence.

title: The Ten Great Signs in One Map
hook: Ten signs, one report: the Hour does not arrive until the world has seen them all.
body: The companions were discussing the Hour when the Prophet ﷺ came upon them and asked what they were saying. Then he gave them the list that this whole room keeps returning to: it will not stand until you see ten signs, the Smoke, the Dajjal, the Beast, the rising of the sun from its setting place, the descent of Isa son of Maryam ﷺ, Yajuj and Majuj, and three sinkings of the earth, one in the east, one in the west, one in the Peninsula of the Arabs, and the last of that a fire emerging from Yemen, driving the people to their place of gathering.

Honesty about this list includes honesty about its order. The transmissions of the same hadith arrange the ten differently, and the report does not number a sequence. What can be ordered is what other evidence orders: the Dajjal, then the descent of Isa ﷺ who ends him, then the release of Yajuj and Majuj, as the account of Muslim 2937 runs; and a narration in Muslim makes the western sunrise, with the Beast at its heels, first among the signs in one respect, a firstness scholars discuss. So this tile is a map, not a timetable: ten certainties, their full sequence left folded.

Four of the ten have their own entries in this room, the Smoke, the Beast, the western sunrise, and Yajuj and Majuj; the Dajjal and the descent of Isa ﷺ carry entire literatures of their own. The three sinkings and the final fire stand in the hadith with almost no added description, and that is how they stand here: named, awaited, and not embroidered.

claims.text: The Hour will not stand until ten signs are seen: the Smoke, the Dajjal, the Beast, the sun rising from its setting place, the descent of Isa son of Maryam ﷺ, Yajuj and Majuj, three sinkings of the earth, and a fire from Yemen driving people to their gathering
Within the ten, the Dajjal, then the descent of Isa ﷺ who ends him, then the release of Yajuj and Majuj follow one another
One narration makes the western sunrise, with the Beast close on its heels, first among the signs in one respect, a firstness scholars discuss
The full order of the ten is not decisively fixed; transmissions of the hadith vary in arrangement, and this room presents the list as a map, not a timetable

evidence.boundary: The sources provide no dates and no complete sequence for the ten, and they do not identify any present event with any sign; only a few relative orders are established.
evidence.note: A variant wording of the hadith has the fire beginning from the depth of Aden.

title: The Serpent of Hoarded Wealth
hook: Wealth that refused its duty returns on the Day as a serpent that says, I am your treasure.
body: The Prophet ﷺ said: whoever Allah gives wealth and he does not pay its zakat, his wealth will be made to appear for him on the Day of Resurrection as a bald headed serpent with two dark marks, it will be wrapped around him like a collar, it will seize him by the corners of his mouth, and it will say, I am your wealth, I am your treasure. Then he recited the verse of Al Imran: let them not think that what they withheld of Allah’s bounty is good for them; they will be collared with what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection.

The Qur’an’s own imagery is fire rather than serpent: those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah are promised a Day when it is heated in the fire of Jahannam and their foreheads, sides, and backs are branded with it, this is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard. In Muslim 987 the hoard becomes plates of fire pressed to the owner through a Day fifty thousand years long, until judgment is passed. The wealth is not lost; it is returned, transformed into testimony.

Read honestly, this is a scene of the Reckoning, not a monster of the world. The hadith’s own verb says the wealth is made to appear so for its keeper on that Day; nothing in the sources sets a serpent loose in the earth before it. The category matters: the terror here is not zoological but moral, the reunion of a person with what he was given and what he withheld. The door out is equally plain, and it is open now: give the wealth its right.

claims.text: Wealth whose zakat was withheld is made to appear on the Day of Resurrection as a bald headed serpent with two dark marks that collars its keeper, seizes his jaws, and says, I am your wealth, I am your treasure
Those who withhold what Allah gave them of His bounty will be collared with it on the Day of Resurrection
Hoarded gold and silver will be heated in the fire of Jahannam and used to brand foreheads, sides, and backs
This is reckoning imagery for the one who refused zakat, wealth given a form on that Day, not a creature said to roam the earth now

evidence.boundary: The sources do not describe a serpent alive in the world today; the scene belongs to the Day of Resurrection and to the one who withheld the right of his wealth.
evidence.note: The hadith’s wording, his wealth will be made to appear for him, fixes this as a scene of the Reckoning, and the entry is categorized accordingly.
